questions.q: A business has total assets of ₦45,000 and total liabilities of ₦15,000. If the owner introduces an additional ₦5,000 cash as capital, what is the new total capital of the business?
questions.explain:
According to the fundamental accounting equation:

$$\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Capital}$$

Initial Capital is determined as:
$$\text{Capital} = \text{Assets} - \text{Liabilities}$$
$$\text{Capital} = ₦45,000 - ₦15,000 = ₦30,000$$

When the owner introduces an additional ₦5,000, this increases both Cash (Asset) and Capital by ₦5,000.
New Capital = ₦30,000 + ₦5,000 = **₦35,000**.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions will result in an increase in both an asset and a liability?
options: Payment of cash to a trade creditor
Purchase of trading goods on credit
Withdrawal of cash from the bank by the owner for personal use
questions.explain:
Let's analyze the effects of each transaction on the accounting equation:
*   **Purchase of trading goods on credit:** Increases stock/inventory (Asset) and increases creditors/payables (Liability). This is the correct answer.
*   *Payment to creditor:* Decreases asset (cash) and decreases liability (creditors).
*   *Cash sales:* Increases one asset (cash) and decreases another (stock) if at cost.
*   *Withdrawals:* Decreases asset (bank) and decreases capital (drawings).
